title: Interest rates and stocks: the rule held fifteen percent of the time
description:
Free options app: https://www.signumhq.com/app?src=yt_us1

"Rates go up, stocks go down." You hear it every day. We counted it.

Every session from 2006 to today: the 10-year Treasury yield against the S&P 500. 4,924 trading days.

Across the whole span the correlation is +0.284, t = 20.75. Not negative. Positive. On average they rose together.

Window by window, same story. Across 4,673 one-year windows the median is +0.348, and the rule held — a negative correlation — in only 15.3%. Windows above +0.5 were more common at 18.2%. The strongest was +0.712 in August 2012.

But today reads -0.306, the bottom 0.1% of the record, nearly level with the all-time low of -0.312 in July 2024. The rule is not wrong. It is conditional, and today you are inside that 15%.

We measured direction only. Why the sign flips is not something we measured, and this is not causation.

Rates are FRED DGS10 daily changes. Stocks are SPY closes.

evidence: FRED DGS10 (US 10-year yield, daily) x FMP stable SPY closes, 2006-10-06 to 2026-08-20, 4,924 overlapping sessions
Metric is the correlation between SPY daily returns and DGS10 daily change in basis points; 252-session rolling windows give 4,673 windows
Full-span correlation +0.284 (t=20.75). Rolling median +0.348, range -0.312 to +0.712, negative in 15.3% of windows, above +0.5 in 18.2%
Current window -0.306 sits at the 0.1st percentile; the record low is -0.312 on 2024-07-08

story.event: As of August 2026 the one-year correlation between US rates and US stocks sits near its lowest reading in twenty years.
story.mechanism: "Rates up, stocks down" is repeated constantly but nobody publishes its hit rate. Over twenty years the sign is usually positive; the rule describes a minority of the record, and today falls inside it.
story.anchor: Held 15.3% of the time; today is the bottom 0.1%

insight.claim: The rates-stocks one-year correlation was negative in only 15.3% of windows since 2006, and today's -0.306 sits at the 0.1st percentile
